requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation has marked code and a test.

**Obligations**
1. Definitions referenced by the subject or any contributed source contribute their complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.
2. Definitions referenced by those definitions are included transitively, without duplicates and without nontermination on cycles.
3. When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same complete transitive set is supplied to the model and recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Code**
- **Obligations 1 and 2, initial set.** `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs) builds the mandatory sources. It then calls `definition_inputs` with those inputs and `Some(&subject.text)`, so terms in the subject text and in every contributed source are covered.
  - `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies` (src/terms.rs). `direct_references` collects terms from the subject text and from each input's text: Rust comments, Markdown, requirements bodies, and definition selectors. `close_dependencies` then computes the transitive closure into a `BTreeSet`, which gives deduplication and handles cycles.
  - `definition_inputs` turns each name into an `InputSelector::Definition` through `source_input`. That produces the model input for the definition.
  - `prepare` appends the results to `mandatory` only if they are not already present.
- **Obligation 3.** `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions` recomputes the closure over the newly delivered inputs and drops definitions already supplied or recorded. The `habeas` read tool (`read` in src/authoring/tools.rs), `search`, `structural` and `declared_query` all call it. Each adds the definitions to the delivered inputs and to the tool result.
  - In `converse` (src/authoring/mod.rs), delivered inputs go into `pending`. After the next response, `record_inputs` records them, and this happens before a submission is parsed. `record_inputs` deduplicates.

**Tests**
- **Subject terms and transitive closure.** `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (inputs.rs) has the subject using `terms.unit`, which uses `terms.value`. It asserts exactly two definition inputs.
- **Contributed-source terms.** `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks that a term referenced by a contributed source is supplied.
- **Additional reads, complete declaration, cycles, ordering.** `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (mod.rs) uses a mutually referencing `unit` and `value` pair, so it covers a cycle. It asserts the following:
  - each definition appears once;
  - the text starts with `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:`;
  - the definitions reach the second request before the submission;
  - the definitions appear in the recorded evidence inputs.
- **Each read tool.** `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` covers the `habeas` item and line-range reads. `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` covers `ripgrep`. `ast_grep_returns_innermost_nodes_of_the_language_and_reports_failures` and `ast_grep_queries_run_declared_queries_and_return_their_sites` cover both `ast_grep` forms.

**Marking and unspecified behavior**
- Relevant code and tests carry `{impl}` or `{test}` references to `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
- `terms::dependencies` and its helpers are marked for the separate `requirements.definitions.dependencies` and `requirements.definitions.selection`. I did not treat that as a marking gap here.
- I found no unspecified behavior.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
